question: Across eight newly rendered consecutive frames, how does frame-to-frame change in scene-linear error relative to a dual-REFERENCE1024 proxy differ among NATURAL32, deterministic Q4 and deterministic Q8?

evidenceBasis.role: single-frame evidence motivates a temporal derivation; it does not supply temporal confirmation

design.sequenceSemantics: each cell-replicate launches one fresh Blender process and renders all frames in ascending order inside that process

analysis.referenceAtFrame: pixelwise mean of REFERENCE1024_A and REFERENCE1024_B
analysis.spatialEdgeMagnitude: RGB Euclidean central-difference gradient magnitude on the reference
analysis.spatialEdgeMaskRule: For both endpoints select exact top 25,920 pixels by magnitude descending then flattened C-row-major index ascending; use their union for the transition.
analysis.motionMagnitude: RGB Euclidean magnitude of reference_t minus reference_t-1
analysis.motionMaskRule: Select exact top 25,920 pixels by magnitude descending then flattened C-row-major index ascending.
metrics: RMSE and maximum absolute temporal error delta per transition and method replicate
mean replicate RMSE for NATURAL32, Q4 and Q8
Q4/NATURAL, Q8/NATURAL and Q8/Q4 RMSE ratios in every domain
REFERENCE1024 A/B temporal residual delta divided by NATURAL32 temporal error-delta mean
Q4 and Q8 composite A/B exactness per frame and transition
observed Blender render seconds by cell

attacksRequired: wrong spec or B32 evidence-basis hash
wrong scene, Blender or OCIO identity
changed frame interval, point set, weights, samples or threads
out-of-order, missing or hash-mismatched EXR output
non-empty work or evidence directory at start
tampered metric, binding or derivation decision
nonClaims: This derivation cannot confirm temporal quality because its observations may be used to freeze a later threshold.
The dual REFERENCE1024 mean is a reference proxy, not ground truth.
Temporal error-delta ratios are not calibrated visibility or cinematic-quality scores.
Motion blur is disabled and the eight-frame interval is one scene on one machine.
A later formal holdout must use a disjoint consecutive-frame interval and entirely new outputs.
Human preference and visible flicker require an independently completed blind review.
